questions: Did your walking difficulty begin gradually and worsen over months or years rather than start suddenly?
Do you feel generally slowed or stiff in your daily activities?
Do you have a tremor in a hand or another limb when it is relaxed?
Do your feet ever feel temporarily “stuck” when you start walking, turn, or pass through a doorway?
Has one side of your body become noticeably slower or stiffer than the other?
Has your arm swing decreased while walking?
Have you had recent falls or near-falls?
Do you have difficulty turning in bed, rising from a chair, or getting out of a car?
Have your handwriting, voice volume, or facial expressions become noticeably smaller or less expressive?
Have you developed urinary urgency or incontinence?
Have you or someone close to you noticed a decline in memory, attention, or thinking?
Are you taking, or have you recently taken, antipsychotic, anti-nausea, or other dopamine-blocking medication?
Do you have numbness, tingling, or loss of position sense in your feet?
Do you have back or neck pain, leg weakness, or electric-shock sensations down your spine or limbs?
Do you have dizziness, slurred speech, double vision, or difficulty coordinating your limbs?
